study_label: BREVACTA: subcutaneous tocilizumab versus placebo in rheumatoid arthritis

objective.value: To characterize the efficacy and safety of subcutaneous tocilizumab (TCZ-SC) 162 mg every other week versus placebo in adults with moderate to severe rheumatoid arthritis with an inadequate response to at least 1 DMARD.

population.value: Adults aged 18 years or older with rheumatoid arthritis for at least 6 months, moderate to severe active disease (swollen joint count at least 6, tender joint count at least 8, radiographic erosion, and elevated CRP and/or ESR), and inadequate response to at least 1 DMARD. Patients had received at least 1 traditional DMARD at a stable dose for at least 8 weeks; up to 20% could have had inadequate response to an anti-TNF agent.

intervention.value: Subcutaneous tocilizumab (TCZ-SC) 162 mg every other week for 24 weeks, randomized 2:1; from week 12, eligible patients could receive escape therapy with TCZ-SC 162 mg weekly at investigator discretion.

comparator.value: Subcutaneous placebo every other week for 24 weeks; from week 12, eligible patients could receive escape therapy with TCZ-SC 162 mg weekly at investigator discretion.

duration_follow_up.value: The double-blind treatment period was 24 weeks, followed by a 72-week open-label period. The primary endpoint was assessed at week 24.

primary_outcome.value: Percentage of patients achieving an American College of Rheumatology 20% improvement response (ACR20) at week 24.

effect_result.value: At week 24, ACR20 response was 60.9% (95% CI 56.3% to 65.4%) with TCZ-SC versus 31.5% (95% CI 25.4% to 37.7%) with placebo. The weighted between-group difference was 29.5 percentage points (95% CI 22.0 to 37.0; P<0.0001).

safety.value: Over 24 weeks, at least 1 adverse event occurred in 62.7% of TCZ-SC and 57.8% of placebo recipients; serious adverse events occurred in 4.6% and 3.7%, respectively. Serious infections occurred in 2.1% and 1.8%; injection-site reactions in 7.1% and 4.1%. Three deaths occurred in the TCZ-SC group and none in the placebo group; all three were reported as related to TCZ treatment.

evidence_questions.population: Adults with moderate to severe rheumatoid arthritis and inadequate response to at least 1 DMARD.
